alloy.preparation: Commercial hot-rolled Type 430 steel; annealed 1 h at 815 °C and water quenched. Acrylic-mounted with the 0.5 × 0.6 cm exposed surface a longitudinal section parallel to the rolled surface; polished by standard metallography to a distilled-water slurry of 0.3 µm alumina; masked with Scotch 470 electroplater tape except for a circular 0.36 cm diameter area for pitting measurements.

test_method.procedure_description: Saturated calomel reference; platinum auxiliary isolated by glass frit. Usually scanned from −0.7 to −0.6 V SCE into the passive region, at 540 mV/hr until approximately 0.1–0.2 V below expected pitting, then slowed tenfold to 54 mV/hr. Stopped at pitting potential and allowed to pit for 20–30 min; tape removed and surface examined for pits and possible crevice corrosion.
test_method.pitting_criterion: Sharp, sudden rise in polarization current, distinguished from the gradual increase associated with crevice corrosion; post-test examination of the free electrode surface.

experiments.result_note: Source-reported average of experimental pitting potentials.

test_method.procedure_description: Actively corroding electrode switched almost instantaneously to a preset noble passive-region potential, +0.40 V SCE, in 0.1 N HCl. This is a distinct potential-jump protocol, not the slow potential scan.
test_method.pitting_criterion: Pitting observed at the imposed +0.40 V; the precise threshold is not established.

experiments.result_note: Pitting observed at the stated imposed potential under a distinct potential-jump protocol. Not an exact threshold and not equivalent to the >0.80v scan bound.
